verdict.rationale: Gitleaks documents its own configuration format (gitleaks.toml) for writing custom secret-detection rules. It also supports composite rules and per-rule allowlists. A config path can be set explicitly via GITLEAKS_CONFIG, which plausibly lets teams point many repos at one shared file. However, the rules cover secret detection only, not general static analysis, and cross-repo sharing is never documented as a feature. Missing for 10: general-purpose static-analysis rule support beyond secrets, documented mechanism for sharing or extending rule sets across repositories, examples of the rule syntax, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can write custom static-analysis rules in a simple syntax and share them across repositories

citations.quote: Gitleaks offers a configuration format you can follow to write your own secret detection rules
In v8.28.0 Gitleaks introduced composite rules, which are made up of a single "primary" rule and one or more auxiliary or `required` rules.
You can define multiple allowlists for a rule to reduce false positives.
You can use `GITLEAKS_CONFIG` to explicitly set a config path _or_ create a `gitleaks.toml` at the root of the repo which will be automatically detected and used by **gitleaks-action**.
